title: Decision making during ambitendency in catatonia
summary:
Catatonia  is a severe alteration of volition (poor decision making) and movements (impaired motor planning and execution) that often—but not always—occurs in connection with another psychiatric illness. 
In extreme forms, patients are in a stuporous state, neither move nor react to external stimuli. However, the catatonia syndrome may present in mild to moderate severity, in which movements are not (yet) affected, but decision making (ambitendency) and motor planning are already impaired. 

This project will explore the neural substrates of decision making under conflict in patients with mild catatonia and current ambitendency using behavioural tests, functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI), non-invasive brain stimulation (Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation - TMS), and changes within-subjects' reported experience during catatonia and remission. 
Furthermore healthy and patient controls (without catatonia) will be tested for comparison.

interventions.name: Patients diagnosed with Catatonia according to three or more ICD-11 criteria, presentation with a BFCRS of < 10 and current ambitendency: Psychomotor tests and clinical assessments, MRI, rTMS/cTBS + Behavioural tests, physiology at baseline,  day 1 and at remission (4 weeks at the latest)
Patient controls without catatonia: Psychomotor tests and clinical assessments, MRI, cortical exciteability measure (TMS), behavioural tests, physiology at baseline,  day 1 and at 4 weeks
Healthy controls: Psychomotor tests and clinical assessments, MRI, cortical exciteability measure (TMS), behavioural tests, physiology at baseline,  day 1 and at 4 weeks

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Project specific: 
- Patients only: Catatonia diagnosis according to 
   ICD-11, presentation with a BFCRS of < 10 and
   current ambitendency. 
- Age: 18 years and above  
- Understanding of the study project, ability and      
   willingness to participate in the study 
- Ability to provide written informed consent 
- Multiple study participation is possible for 
   catatonia patients if patients present with a
   novel catatonia episode following remission of 
   the previous one
- Clinical/patient controls only:  matched    
   underlying disorder (without catatonia),  
   matched for age and gender
Exclusion criteria:
- Specific contraindicators that exclude for MRI   
  and/or TMS measures:
  E.g. Medical or metal implants (pacemaker) that   
  are not MRI/TMS-safe, claustrophobia,      
  pregnancy, hearing problems/Tinnitus
- Healthy controls only: own history of any severe 
  psychiatric illness or first-degree relatives with 
  Psychotic disorders (Bipolar, Schizophrenia)
- Clinical/patient controls only: own history of 
   catatonia
